stem:
The diagram shows Arjun's circuit: one cell, an open switch, and a lamp joined in a single series path. He wants a circuit diagram of the same loop using standard symbols.

Which claims about that circuit diagram are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Each part must use its standard symbol: the cell as a long line and a short line, the open switch as a break in the wire, and the lamp as a circle with a cross.
The series connections must match the loop even if the lamp is drawn on the other side of the page.
The lamp may be drawn as a circle marked A, because any neat circle is fine for a light-maker.
The cell should be drawn with two parallel lamp branches, so the switch and the lamp each get their own loop.

teacher.key_rationale: A circuit diagram must use standard symbols and keep the same series connections. Drawing the lamp as an ammeter circle swaps the symbol. Adding parallel branches changes the circuit topology.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source cylinders/clips into a simple labeled cell–open switch–lamp series loop.
